name: inprocess-obi-apb-axi4lite-mixed-timer-axiluart-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches two targets of different protocols by address in one process: the PULP timer as an APB3 register target (the one F5 target) and the ZipCPU axiluart as an AXI4-Lite register target. Each target states its own protocol from its own artifact, and each case states the protocol of the target it was routed to.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches two independently addressed MMIO targets of different protocols in one process instead of one CPU x IP wiring: target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000 behind the real apb3_mmio_bridge (profile protocol apb/3), target 1 is the ZipCPU axiluart at 0x40002000 behind the real axi4_lite_mmio_bridge (profile protocol axi4-lite/1).

The timer window is the profile's own 4 KiB APB3 window; the AXI4-Lite slave's window is the 16 bytes its C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH=4 boundary decodes. 0x40001000..0x40002000 and 0x40002000..0x40002010 do not overlap, neither overlaps the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000, and both clear the 4 GiB bound.
Timer registers: TIMER0_COUNT(0), TIMER0_CTRL(4), TIMER0_CMP(8). axiluart registers: SETUP(0, rw), FIFO_STATUS(4, ro), RXREG(8, rw, read pops the RX FIFO), TXREG(12, rw, write pushes the TX FIFO).

Only target 0 declares F5 facts, through configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json: irq_o[0], a 16-tick pulse, trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,4294967295]] and the TIMER0_COUNT status word at offset 0. The F5 target must be APB3 in this increment; an AXI4-Lite target that declares the four F5 facts is still refused by name (now unsupported-f5:target-protocol-not-run:axi4-lite:<name>, because no real AXI4-Lite F5 run exists) instead of being given an untested path.

The axiluart declares no F5 facts here on purpose: its four interrupt outputs are level sources of FIFO occupancy or received-serial activity, and none is raised by a write to a declared register. The target is reached by address for F2/F4 only, and the summary states target1_f5 no.

rx=1 and cts_n=0 are the same pin constants the single-target AXI4-Lite scenario declares; the duplication between fixed_inputs and tuning.fixed_inputs is intentional, because the target request builder reads tuning and the generated header reads fixed_inputs.

No DMA is declared in this scenario: the AXI4-Lite target has no DMA route in this increment, and a DMA route to an AXI4-Lite target is refused by name (unsupported-dma-route:apb3-target-only:...). F6 is therefore refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:...
The three profiles declare 50 MHz each, so one host tick drives all three models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.

The F5 case line's trigger/status words are the APB3 target's (apb_* in a one-protocol APB3 build, the protocol-neutral target_* group in this mixed build), and the case states target_protocol apb3, so the F5 words follow the selected F5 target rather than a build-wide word.
